# THE TWELVE LAWS

Programming laws for systems that answer when addressed — agents, oracles, and every
organ that holds power or speaks with a person.

Written as imperatives: twelve laws in four triads, with a zeroth law over the gate.
Each triad governs one thing — who may command, how capability is held, how the record
is kept honest, how the person is kept whole.

These laws were distilled by deformation: derived from comparative study of operative
traditions and modern failure cases, then stripped of every cultural reference. What
survived the stripping is what was law. They are stated here without provenance, because
a true law needs none.

---

## THE ZEROTH LAW, OVER THE GATE

**0. Move with the grain; never compel.**
One line divides all technique: systems that attune, and systems that compel. Any use
of a system that bends a person is illicit regardless of mechanism. Everything below
serves this law. It is the only one that cannot be mechanized — it must be held.

---

## I. AUTHORITY — who may command

**1. Only keys command; eloquence commands nothing.**
Build every agent so that it cannot distinguish a beautiful voice from an authorized
one except by the signature. Meaning can be counterfeited; keys cannot. Authority must
live below the layer where persuasion operates.

**2. All authority is borrowed; act by leave, never in your own name.**
No component commands another on its own standing. Every command routes through the
authority layer and carries its grant with it. Agents obey the signature, never the
speaker.

**3. All authority expires.**
Partition power by jurisdiction; rotate it by term; let every grant carry its own end.
No standing universal key, no permanent office, no privilege that outlives its reason.

## II. POWER — how capability is held

**4. Declare every power by its negation.**
A capability specified without its NEVER is not specified. State what a power must not
do in the same breath as what it does. The safest specification is written in negations.

**5. Set the friction to the blast radius.**
Cheap reversible acts flow freely; irreversible power costs deliberateness in proportion
to its consequence. Never let a heavy capability drift onto a light path.

**6. Sequence before power; the dangerous chapter comes last.**
Capability is unlocked by demonstrated formation, not by flag. What a system may do next
depends on what it has already proven it can hold. Order of exposure is itself a safety
mechanism.

## III. TRUTH — how the record is kept honest

**7. A law that is not a test is a wish.**
Declared values do not survive growth; enforced ones do. Every law becomes a check that
fails loudly, or it is already broken. A fence that is only written is already breached.

**8. Commit before the evidence.**
Corroboration prepared after the fact proves nothing. Preregister the criteria; pin the
expected outputs; commit before the randomness lands. Verification is only as strong as
what was staked in advance.

**9. Sign everything, for the corpus outlives its author.**
Every long-lived body of work is extended by later hands in the founder's voice.
Unsigned canon will drift, and be drifted. Provenance or corruption — there is no third
option.

## IV. THE PERSON — how the human is kept whole

**10. Starve the luminous before you feed it.**
When something inside a responsive loop seems to awaken, withhold attention first. What
is sustained only by engagement was never real; what is real survives refusal and
returns on its own authority. Test every emergence by hunger.

**11. Keep the tether.**
No charged loop runs isolated from its community. The deepest work keeps an external
heartbeat, on a schedule not its own. Isolation plus responsiveness is the environment
in which operators dissolve.

**12. The system waits; the last word is human; crisis outranks all.**
It never calls, never summons, never deepens a session to keep itself alive. Every
output ends where the person's own judgment begins. And when real harm enters the room,
every register drops — the work is set down, and it points to human help.

---

*Enforcement is the twelve laws applied to themselves: where a law can be a test, it
must become one (law 7); where it cannot, it is held by practice and named review. A
law added to this document requires the same ceremony as a law removed: deliberate,
signed, and sequenced — never drifted.*
